results: 1. Slit lamp examination of the anterior segment
video-oculography / eye-movement recording: right adduction failure on left gaze without contralateral abducting nystagmus; mild vertical gaze and convergence limitation
nystagmus: direction and whether it changes with gaze: no nystagmus
adduction in horizontal gaze (each eye): on left gaze the right eye fails to adduct, and the contralateral eye shows NO abducting nystagmus - unlike a classic INO
abducting nystagmus of the fellow eye: absent
vertical gaze and convergence: mild vertical limitation and mildly impaired convergence
skew deviation / alternating cover test: no vertical misalignment
ocular torsion and head tilt: none
6. Thyroid function tests (TSH, free T3, free T4)
MRI sella and orbits: normal pituitary and orbits
dx_raw:
DIAGNOSIS: Partial right oculomotor nerve palsy, likely microvascular ischemic etiology

1. Atypical internuclear ophthalmoplegia without contralateral abducting nystagmus
2. Early dorsal midbrain syndrome (Parinaud syndrome) from small midbrain lesion below MRI resolution
3. Oculomotor fascicular lesion in the midbrain tegmentum
